decisions.rationale: Lead Mega Alakazam and Floette-Eternal for immediate speed and high special-pressure options into the opponent’s likely sand lead; bring Garchomp and Milotic as durable backline answers to Tyranitar, Excadrill, and Steel-types. This avoids Talonflame’s dangerous exposure to repeated Rock Slide.
decisions.notebook: Opponent previously led Tyranitar–Excadrill in game 1 for immediate Sand Stream plus Sand Rush pressure. Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect; Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Expect Focus Sash on Excadrill and respect sand speed; Mega Alakazam can potentially gain valuable ability utility on evolution. Avoid pairing Talonflame and Garchomp into the opponent’s Rock Slide-heavy sand core.

decisions.rationale: Sand core lead (Tyranitar+Excadrill) remains strongest: Excadrill's Steel typing resists both Fake Out (0.5x) and Brave Bird (0.5x), making opponent's priority disruption ineffective. Focus Sash provides backup safety. Sand Stream triggers on entry so sand is active even if Tyranitar is flinched. Back: Gholdengo for Fake Out immunity + Good as Gold status blocking (switch-in vs Scrafty Snarl/Taunt), and Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag as late-game win condition to trap weakened foes. Opponent likely adapts with Scrafty/Milotic but Excadrill under sand outspeedes their entire team except Alakazam-Mega Trace (which cannot KO Excadrill).
decisions.notebook: G2: Opponent likely adapts to sand with Scrafty (Intimidate/Fake Out) and/or Milotic (Competitive/Icy Wind). Key discovery: Excadrill's Steel typing makes both Fake Out (0.5x) and Brave Bird (0.5x) NVE, so priority disruption is far less threatening than expected. Excadrill can Protect (pri +4) before Fake Out (pri +3) to avoid flinch. Sand Stream triggers on switch-in/entry, so sand is active even if Tyranitar is flinched. Gholdengo is Ghost (Fake Out immune) + Good as Gold (blocks Snarl/Taunt/status) — ideal Scrafty switch-in. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag for late-game trapping. Alakazam-Mega Trace under sand copies Sand Rush (374+ Spe) but cannot KO Excadrill (Shadow Ball max 42%, Psychic NVE). Plan: Protect Excadrill T1 if priority expected, sweep T2 under sand. Watch for Tailwind from Talonflame — under Tailwind, Talonflame (187+ Spe) can outspeed Excadrill under sand (280). If Tailwind goes up, consider switching to Gholdengo or playing defensively.

decisions.rationale: Protect Mega Alakazam while pivoting Floette into Milotic: this denies the opponents’ immediate dual KO routes and brings in a bulkier answer to the sand core. Mega Evolution also gives Alakazam an immediate chance to copy Sand Rush for future speed control.
decisions.notebook: Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect; Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash with Sand Rush, Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect. Their standard sand lead creates immediate Sand Rush pressure. Preserve Floette for its strong Fairy pressure into Tyranitar; use Mega Alakazam’s Trace opportunistically for Sand Rush speed control.

decisions.rationale: Crunch Alakazam (SE, possible OHKO 89-195%) and Iron Head Floette (SE, possible OHKO 86-169%). Both attacks are super-effective with OHKO potential. Even if one foe Protects, the other takes massive damage. Tyranitar survives Floette's Light of Ruin (49-70%) and Alakazam's Shadow Ball is negligible on Tyranitar (5-7%) or non-KO on Excadrill (30-42%, Focus Sash safe). This is the highest-EV aggressive opening that punishes the opponent for not Protecting while still being acceptable if they do.
decisions.notebook: G2 T1: Confirmed damage ranges — Excadrill Iron Head vs Floette 86-169% (possible OHKO), Tyranitar Crunch vs Alakazam 89-195% (possible OHKO), Floette Light of Ruin vs Tyranitar 49-70% (not KO), Alakazam Shadow Ball vs Tyranitar 5-7% (NVE negligible), vs Excadrill 30-42% (not KO, Focus Sash safe). Alakazam-Mega Trace under sand copies Sand Rush (374+ Spe) but cannot KO Excadrill through Focus Sash. Plan: if both foes survive T1, finish them T2 with Excadrill outspeeding everything. If one foe is KO'd, expect a switch-in — Scrafty (Intimidate) or Milotic (Competitive) likely. Gholdengo remains the ideal switch-in for Scrafty's Snarl/Knock Off. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag saved for late-game trapping. Watch for Tailwind from Talonflame if it switches in — under Tailwind, Talonflame outspeeds Excadrill under sand.

decisions.rationale: Pivot Alakazam out of the guaranteed Crunch KO into Floette, which resists Crunch, while Icy Wind cuts both foes’ Speed and removes Excadrill’s Sand Rush tempo for the following turn.
decisions.notebook: Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect. Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash with Sand Rush, Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Preserve Mega Alakazam from Tyranitar Crunch; use Milotic speed control to neutralize Sand Rush, then pressure Excadrill with Alakazam and Milotic while Floette checks Tyranitar.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill is the opponent's mandatory kill target (only 280 Speed mon, Focus Sash, 205 Atk). They will likely double-target it with Scald+Shadow Ball, which KOes through Sash since Shadow Ball chips first. Protecting Excadrill wastes their double-target while Tyranitar Crunch (74-149% of max vs 93% HP) likely KOes Alakazam-Mega. Even if Crunch falls short, Alakazam drops to ~19% and is finished next turn. Excadrill preserved at 100% with Sash is our win condition for the remaining matchup.
decisions.notebook: G2 T2: Confirmed — Milotic Scald vs Excadrill 68-103% (possible OHKO, Focus Sash saves only first hit). If both foes target Excadrill, Shadow Ball (30-42%) + Scald (68-103%) KOes through Sash since second hit lands on non-full HP. Opponent's optimal play is double-targeting Excadrill. Tyranitar Crunch vs Alakazam at 93%: 74-149% of max, ~75% KO chance. High Horsepower vs Milotic: 37-71%, cannot KO from 82%. Plan: Protect Excadrill when double-target is likely; finish Alakazam T2, then 2v1 vs Milotic. Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag saved for late-game. Watch for opponent switching Alakazam to Scrafty (Intimidate) if they predict Crunch.

decisions.rationale: Floette must Protect against Excadrill’s guaranteed Iron Head KO. Milotic’s Scald pressures Excadrill, can heavily chip or burn it, and avoids letting its Focus Sash remain fully intact for later.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect and Sand Stream. Opponent Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Preserve Mega Alakazam from Tyranitar Crunch; use Milotic speed control and Water pressure to neutralize Excadrill, while Floette checks Tyranitar. Opponent’s unrevealed back line is two of Gengar, Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, and Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill Iron Head guarantees KO on Floette at 65% (86-169% range, outspeeds at 280). Floette cannot attack this turn — it either Protects (can't act) or is KOed before acting. Tyranitar Crunch chips Milotic for 24-46%, advancing toward a 2HKO range. Milotic most likely Scalds Excadrill (break Sash, remove fast threat), making Crunch free damage. Even if Milotic targets Tyranitar (24-36%), Tyranitar survives at 60-72% and remains functional. If Floette Protects, Crunch still chips Milotic — no wasted turn. Pressing advantage while up 1-0 in series.
decisions.notebook: Excadrill Iron Head guaranteed KO on Floette from 65%+. Tyranitar Crunch 24-46% Milotic (neutral STAB). Milotic Scald 24-36% Tyranitar, 68-103% Excadrill (Sash saves). Floette Moonblast 33-49% Tyranitar, Light of Ruin 49-71% — neither KOs from 96%. Excadrill Rock Slide 20-40% Floette (cannot KO from 65%). Plan: KO Floette T3, chip Milotic into 2HKO range. If Excadrill Sash is broken (1 HP), switch to Gholdengo or Gengar-Mega next turn. Save Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag for late-game trapping. Watch for 4th Pokémon reveal when Floette falls or switches.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill acts before Floette and can OHKO it, while Scald is a guaranteed KO on the 25% Excadrill if it does not Protect. Light of Ruin maximally punishes an Excadrill Protect by threatening a Tyranitar KO or leaving it severely weakened; Floette is otherwise likely being traded for Excadrill.
Bring in Garchomp to immediately threaten Tyranitar with Ground damage; Mega Alakazam cannot safely face Tyranitar's revealed Crunch.
decisions.notebook: Opponent Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock with Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect. Opponent Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect. Preserve Mega Alakazam from Tyranitar Crunch; Garchomp provides the immediate Ground pressure into Tyranitar. Opponent’s unrevealed back line is two of Gengar, Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, and Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Excadrill outspeeds everything (280 Speed) and Iron Head is a guaranteed KO on Floette at 59% (SE 2×). KOing Floette removes the biggest threat to Tyranitar (all Floette damaging moves are SE on Tyranitar). Tyranitar Crunches Milotic for 24–46% STAB chip, putting it in easy 2HKO/KO range for next turn. Excadrill will likely fall to Milotic's Scald afterward, but trading a 25% Sash-broken Excadrill for Floette at 59% plus heavy Milotic chip is an excellent exchange. If Milotic instead Recovers, Excadrill survives and we maintain pressure. Tyranitar at 96% can tank any hit from the 4th Pokémon that switches in after Floette falls.
decisions.notebook: Excadrill Iron Head guaranteed KO on Floette from 65%+ HP. Tyranitar Crunch 24-46% Milotic (neutral STAB). Milotic Scald 24-36% Tyranitar, 68-103% Excadrill (Sash already broken at 25%). Floette Moonblast 33-49% Tyranitar, Light of Ruin 49-71%. Save Gengar-Mega Shadow Tag for late-game trapping after opponent's team is thinned. Gholdengo good as gold immune to status moves, Steel/Ghost resists Fairy. Watch for 4th Pokémon reveal when Floette falls — Garchomp (LO EQ), Talonflame (Gale Wings BB), or Scrafty (Intimidate/Fake Out) are the options.

decisions.rationale: Bring Gengar to replace Excadrill. Gengar is neutral to Ground, neutralizing the Garchomp Earthquake threat that would hit both Tyranitar (2x) and Gholdengo (2x) as a spread move. Gengar outspeeds Garchomp (178 vs 134-169) with 4x Icy Wind. Gholdengo saved on bench for a clean switch-in vs Alakazam-Mega later (resists Psychic, immune to Taunt via Good as Gold). Tyranitar stays in to pressure Milotic at 28% with Crunch. Alakazam-Mega threatens Gengar with 2x Shadow Ball but is single-target and Gengar at 100% should survive one hit.
decisions.notebook: Gengar (Ghost/Poison) neutral to Ground; Gholdengo (Steel/Ghost) weak to Ground and Dark. Gengar Icy Wind 4x vs Garchomp, 2x vs Talonflame; Shadow Ball 2x vs Alakazam-Mega. Gholdengo resists Psychic and immune to status moves (Good as Gold) — best Alakazam-Mega switch-in. Mega Gengar Shadow Tag traps all opponent Pokémon (none Ghost-type). Alakazam-Mega has Trace (copied Sand Stream turn 1). Plan: save Gholdengo for Alakazam-Mega matchup; Mega Evolve Gengar for Shadow Tag when opponent is thinned.

decisions.rationale: Stomping Tantrum guarantees an OHKO on Gengar if Garchomp gets to act, while Protect preserves the low-HP Milotic from likely targeting and avoids Earthquake ally damage.
decisions.notebook: Gengar is Timid with Gengarite, Cursed Body, Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Icy Wind, and Protect; it can Mega Evolve into Shadow Tag Gengar. Tyranitar is Careful Smooth Rock Sand Stream with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, and Protect. Excadrill is Adamant Focus Sash Sand Rush with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, and Protect. Garchomp's Ground pressure is the main immediate answer to Tyranitar and Gengar; preserve Mega Alakazam from Tyranitar's Crunch when possible. Opponent's remaining unrevealed selection is drawn from Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, and Rotom.

decisions.rationale: Garchomp Earthquake is a guaranteed OHKO on Gengar, so Gengar must Protect. Mega Evolving now grants Shadow Tag, trapping both foes — Garchomp cannot switch to Alakazam-Mega. Tyranitar Ice Punch hits Garchomp for 4x (55.8-100.5%, possible OHKO). If Garchomp Protects, Ice Punch is wasted but Shadow Tag is active and next turn Icy Wind + Ice Punch finishes a trapped Garchomp. If Garchomp Earthquakes instead, Tyranitar survives (54-80% from 96%) and then Ice Punches. This is the safest path to removing the biggest threat while gaining permanent trapping value.
decisions.notebook: Garchomp Earthquake guaranteed OHKO on Gengar (149-216%); Gengar must Protect when Garchomp is active and not Protected. Tyranitar Ice Punch 55.8-100.5% vs Garchomp (possible OHKO). Mega Gengar Speed ~200 (base 130 Timid), outspeeds Garchomp but not necessarily Alakazam-Mega (187-222). Shadow Tag traps all opponent Pokemon (none Ghost-type). Plan: Mega Evolve Gengar behind Protect for Shadow Tag, then trap and eliminate Garchomp with Icy Wind + Ice Punch. Save Gholdengo for Alakazam-Mega (resists Psychic, immune to status via Good as Gold). Milotic at 28% is Crunchable (24.3-45.9%) but lower priority than Garchomp.

decisions.rationale: Double-target Mega Gengar: Stomping Tantrum plus Scald guarantees its removal if both attacks connect, while leaving Milotic alive rather than sacrificing it to Earthquake. Removing Gengar is the highest-value immediate line despite its reduced-rate Protect chance.
decisions.notebook: Opponent revealed sets: Timid Mega Gengar with Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Icy Wind, Protect; Careful Smooth Rock Tyranitar with Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect; Adamant Focus Sash Excadrill with Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Remaining game-2 selection is one of Gholdengo, Grimmsnarl, or Rotom. Mega Gengar is highly vulnerable to Garchomp Ground attacks; Tyranitar's sand-boosted special bulk makes Milotic Scald relatively weak. Preserve Mega Alakazam when possible against Tyranitar Crunch.

decisions.rationale: Send in Mega Alakazam; it can immediately threaten the burned Mega Gengar while outspeeding both revealed foes.
decisions.notebook: Game 2 opponent’s revealed sets: Timid Mega Gengar (Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Icy Wind, Protect), Careful Smooth Rock Tyranitar (Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect), and Adamant Focus Sash Excadrill (Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect). Their fourth is one of Leftovers Modest Gholdengo, Light Clay Adamant Prankster Grimmsnarl, or Sitrus Timid Levitate Rotom. Mega Alakazam is the remaining win condition; avoid exposing it unnecessarily to Tyranitar Crunch.

decisions.rationale: Gengar outspeeds Garchomp and KOs it with 4x SE Icy Wind (guaranteed from 11%). Icy Wind also chips Milotic 5-8.2%, and Tyranitar's Crunch (24.3-45.9%) combined with that chip guarantees the KO on Milotic at 28% (min total 29.3% > 28%). Even if one foe Protects, the other still falls; only a rare double Protect stalls us, and Shadow Tag keeps both trapped regardless.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Speed 200 outspeeds Garchomp (134-169) but not guaranteed vs Alakazam-Mega (187-222). Shadow Tag traps all opponent Pokemon (none Ghost-type). Garchomp Earthquake guaranteed OHKO on Gengar. Gholdengo saved for Alakazam-Mega (resists Psychic, immune to status via Good as Gold). Alakazam-Mega has Sand Stream (Traced from Tyranitar) and is at 93%. When Garchomp faints, Alakazam-Mega is forced in. Milotic has Competitive (raises SpAtk on stat drops) — avoid Icy Wind SpAtk drops if Milotic survives. Tyranitar Speed -1 from Icy Wind (turn 2).

decisions.rationale: Psychic guarantees the KO on Mega Gengar before it can move and is the strongest available immediate line.
decisions.notebook: Mega Gengar’s revealed set is Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Icy Wind, Protect; Tyranitar’s is Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect. Mega Alakazam must avoid being left exposed to Tyranitar’s Crunch whenever possible.

decisions.rationale: Opponent has only Alakazam-Mega (93%) left. Gengar at 14% burned is guaranteed KO'd by any Alakazam attack, and speed order is uncertain (187-222 vs 200). Switching Gengar to Gholdengo (100%) is strictly safer: if Alakazam Protects, I still have a dominant 2v1; if it attacks the switch-in slot, Gholdengo survives at high HP; if it targets Tyranitar, Psychic is immune and Shadow Ball NVE. Tyranitar Crunch (SE 2x, 74-149%) may KO outright given Timid Alakazam's likely low defense investment. Even if Crunch falls short, Gholdengo+Tyranitar vs damaged Alakazam next turn is an easy win.
decisions.notebook: Gengar-Mega Speed 200 outspeeds Garchomp (134-169) but not guaranteed vs Alakazam-Mega (187-222). Shadow Tag traps all opponent Pokemon (none Ghost-type). Garchomp Earthquake guaranteed OHKO on Gengar. Gholdengo saved for Alakazam-Mega (resists Psychic, immune to status via Good as Gold). Alakazam-Mega has Sand Stream (Traced from Tyranitar) and is at 93%. When Garchomp faints, Alakazam-Mega is forced in. Milotic has Competitive (raises SpAtk on stat drops) — avoid Icy Wind SpAtk drops if Milotic survives. Tyranitar Speed -1 from Icy Wind (turn 2). Gengar Shadow Ball does 79-147.7% to Alakazam-Mega; Tyranitar Crunch does 74.1-149.2%. Alakazam Psychic/Shadow Ball both guaranteed KO on 14% Gengar. Gholdengo is Steel/Ghost: resists Psychic (0.5x) but weak to Shadow Ball (2x) from Alakazam.

reflections.summary: The 0-2 series loss is authoritative; only Game 2 evidence is available, so the effect of any between-game adjustment versus Game 1 cannot be determined. In Game 2, Milotic successfully removed Excadrill, but the trade cost Floette and left Tyranitar largely intact. Tyranitar's Ice Punch heavily crippled Garchomp, then Gengar's Icy Wind KOed it and Tyranitar's repeated Crunch removed Milotic. This left Mega Alakazam exposed to Tyranitar and facing Gholdengo, which resisted its final Psychic. The brought four had a workable Milotic answer to Excadrill, but Mega Alakazam, Floette, and Garchomp were all poorly positioned into the opponent's revealed Tyranitar pressure and late Gengar/Gholdengo endgame. Mega Alakazam was not a favorable evolution choice once Tyranitar remained healthy, although the available evidence does not establish that Mega Floette would have produced a better result. Preparation was mixed: Milotic fit the matchup well, while the six's shown tools did not establish a reliable plan to preserve pressure against Tyranitar plus Mega Gengar and Gholdengo. Talonflame and Scrafty were available but their sets and matchup value were not revealed, so there is insufficient evidence to claim the full roster offered a materially better four.
reflections.adjustment: For a future series, build the four and Mega choice around a concrete answer to Tyranitar surviving the early exchange and to the Gengar/Gholdengo backline. Do not allow Mega Alakazam to become the last meaningful attacker while Tyranitar can freely Crunch it. Preserve the Tyranitar answer rather than trading all of the team's relevant pieces merely to remove Excadrill, and account for Ice Punch when deploying Garchomp. Re-evaluate Talonflame and Scrafty in testing, but do not assume either is an improvement without confirming their sets and their ability to cover this specific sand-plus-Ghost/Steel structure.
reflections.notebook: Game 2 revealed a Tyranitar/Excadrill lead with Mega Gengar and Gholdengo in back; treat that as a demonstrated line, not a guaranteed habit. Tyranitar: Smooth Rock, Sand Stream, Rock Slide, Crunch, Ice Punch, Protect; it repeatedly used Crunch and retained high HP after the Excadrill trade. Excadrill: Focus Sash, Sand Rush, Iron Head, Rock Slide, High Horsepower, Protect. Mega Gengar: Shadow Ball, Sludge Bomb, Icy Wind, Protect. Gholdengo: Leftovers, Make It Rain, Shadow Ball, Protect, Recover. Milotic was effective into Excadrill and Competitive punished Gengar's Icy Wind, but it could still be finished by Tyranitar's Crunch. Mega Alakazam must not be left exposed to Tyranitar's Crunch, and Garchomp must respect revealed Ice Punch. Prep priority: retain a durable Tyranitar plan while maintaining endgame pressure into Mega Gengar and Gholdengo.

reflections.summary: Won game 2 and the series 2-0 through effective sand-core pressure and a well-executed Gholdengo answer to Mega Alakazam. Tyranitar's Ice Punch proved decisive against Garchomp, and Crunch consistently wore down Milotic and Alakazam. Excadrill traded itself for Floette-Eternal, which was an acceptable exchange given Floette's Fairy typing threatened Gengar. Gengar-Mega's Icy Wind removed Garchomp with a critical hit, and Gholdengo's switch-in on turn 7 perfectly absorbed Alakazam's Psychic while Tyranitar finished it off. The main risk was triggering Milotic's Competitive with Icy Wind, but Tyranitar KO'd it the same turn, neutralizing the threat. No decision errors were recorded; piloting was clean.
reflections.adjustment: The four brought (Tyranitar, Excadrill, Gengar-Mega, Gholdengo) and the Mega Gengar choice were well-suited to this opponent. In a future series, consider whether Grimmsnarl's screens could protect Excadrill from Scald, potentially preserving it longer. Otherwise, the core plan is sound; keep Ice Punch on Tyranitar for Garchomp and maintain Gholdengo as the Alakazam switch-in. Avoid Icy Wind on Milotic unless it will be KO'd the same turn, as Competitive doubles its SpAtk.
reflections.notebook: Opponent tends to bring Mega Alakazam, Milotic, Floette-Eternal, and Garchomp as a four; Talonflame and Scrafty were left behind both games. Mega Alakazam Traces Sand Stream from Tyranitar on entry — weather control can be stolen. Milotic has Competitive: avoid stat drops unless KOing it same turn. Floette-Eternal is weak to Steel (Iron Head) and carries Moonblast/Light of Ruin/Energy Ball. Garchomp runs Stomping Tantrum over Earthquake in this slot and Life Orb. Opponent uses Protect predictably on predicted incoming hits. Tyranitar Ice Punch is the key Garchomp answer; Gholdengo is the reliable Alakazam switch-in (resists Psychic, immune to status). Sand core (Tyranitar + Excadrill) is effective but Excadrill is vulnerable to Scald; Focus Sash mitigates but Water weakness is exploitable. Gengar-Mega outspeeds Garchomp but not Mega Alakazam. Opponent plays protect-heavy and reactive; aggressive double-targets can punish.
